c3_pull_baseline.evidence: First numeric pull baseline on the bess path (0.3.0 recorded none in-repo), docker flow on the CI kernel via the daemon (WEB_UP ~60 s, COW boot): fresh alpine:3.19 pull 29 s, alpine:3.20 pull 33 s (approx 0.11 MB/s compressed incl. layer extract); manifest-only busybox:1.36 re-check 10 s. Registry path confirmed bidirectional (DNS, TLS, layer fetch).

c3_inbound_exposure.evidence: OPEN ISSUE: with an exposure registered (expose 8123 8123 -> 127.0.0.1:8123 -> 192.168.127.2:8123) and a published container listener (-p 8123:80 busybox httpd), every fresh TCP connect from the phone receives gvproxy's 'gvproxy-bess-ok' banner (15 bytes) and closes -- the forwarder never hands the connection to the guest. Outbound NAT works in the same session (pulls). This contradicts the 2026-10-27 cap8 inbound success on port 8123. Suspects: banner-on-unreachable-backend semantics of this gvproxy build vs a regression (COW boot / bess socket path). Next: guest-side 'ip neigh' + packet capture on the bess stream, compare boot configs. NOT a merge-blocker: outbound paths (pull/run/logs) unaffected.

boot.evidence: CI kernel+stub boots the docker flow via the daemon to WEB_UP_MARKER in ~60 s (COW ephemeral boot); clean console poweroff landed after 1.0 s, 0 orphan processes.
